events.title: M7.7 Earthquake Strikes 68km NNW of Ende
events.detail: At 05:58 WITA (21:58 UTC, 14 August) on Saturday 15 August 2026, a shallow magnitude 7.7 earthquake ruptured the Flores Back-Arc Thrust roughly 68 km north-northwest of Ende, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province, at a depth of about 10 km. USGS measured it at Mww 7.7; BMKG initially reported magnitude 7.0 before revising upward to 7.7. Germany's GFZ Helmholtz Centre put it at Mw 7.61 at 25 km depth. Shaking was felt across Flores, Lombok, Sumbawa and parts of South and Southeast Sulawesi.

events.title: BMKG Issues Tsunami Warning Within 2 Minutes 16 Seconds
events.detail: BMKG issued a tsunami warning just 2 minutes and 16 seconds after the mainshock, covering East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces — a response time officials cited as evidence of an improved early-warning system since the catastrophic 1992 Flores tsunami.

events.title: Small Tsunami Waves Recorded at 16 Locations in Four Provinces
events.detail: Localized tsunami waves reached a maximum of 1.61 m at Reok (Manggarai Regency), 0.94 m at Maurole District (Ende Regency), 0.30 m at Labuan Bajo and 0.17 m at Dompu, recorded across roughly 16 coastal monitoring points spanning East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi — far below the 26-metre run-ups seen in the 1992 Flores tsunami.

events.title: Tsunami Warning Lifted After ~3 Hours
events.detail: BMKG lifted the tsunami warning at approximately 07:30 WIB, roughly three hours after the mainshock, after monitoring detected no further dangerous sea-level rise. The Labuan Bajo Harbormaster (KSOP) reopened sailing the same afternoon.

events.title: Death Toll Climbs From 2 to 47 Within Hours
events.detail: Early reports from CGTN put the confirmed death toll at 2, but the figure climbed rapidly through the day as rescue teams reached collapsed buildings — reaching 14 (Karmactive), then 38 (HNGN/Travelers Today), then 47 (Al Jazeera, ABC News, NBC News) by Saturday evening, illustrating how fast-moving and provisional early casualty counts were.
events.confidenceReason: Casualty figures were revised multiple times within the same day as search-and-rescue teams reached remote areas.

events.title: TNI Deploys 1,267 Personnel; Air Force Flies Aid From Kupang
events.detail: The Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI) deployed 1,267 personnel to assist emergency operations on Flores. The Indonesian Air Force mobilized three aircraft to ferry aid from El Tari Airport in Kupang to affected areas, while five helicopters, several planes, a naval vessel and search-and-rescue ships were also committed.

events.title: Prabowo Dispatches 50,000 Presidential Aid Packages
events.detail: President Prabowo Subianto ordered 50,000 presidential aid packages of basic necessities — roughly 275 tonnes of supplies — dispatched to East Nusa Tenggara on the day of the quake, ahead of Indonesia's Independence Day.

events.title: 986 Tourists Evacuated From Padar Island
events.detail: 986 tourists stranded on Padar Island inside Komodo National Park were evacuated to Labuan Bajo after the port authority lifted its suspension of maritime transport services following the earthquake and tsunami alert.

events.title: Frans Sales Lega Airport Ceiling Partially Collapses in Ruteng
events.detail: The terminal ceiling at Frans Sales Lega Airport in Ruteng (Manggarai Regency) partially collapsed during the mainshock. Wings Air subsequently cancelled flights through 22 August while safety inspections continued.

events.title: Shaking Unclogs Hydrothermal Vents at Sano Nggoang Crater Lake
events.detail: Seismic shaking from the mainshock unclogged submerged hydrothermal vents beneath Sano Nggoang crater lake in West Manggarai Regency, sending deep magmatic fluids rich in hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and heavy metals to the surface. On contact with oxygen the H2S oxidized into elemental sulfur and sulfuric acid, turning the lake black and driving its pH down to about 3.17 — a well-understood hydrothermal response to seismic activity rather than a new eruption, according to volcanologists, but one posing a localized toxic-gas hazard.
events.confidenceReason: Reported by a single outlet citing geologists; not yet corroborated by BMKG or a volcanological survey statement.

era: Death Toll Climbs, Rescue Operations Expand (16–17 August 2026)

events.title: Toll Reaches 51 as Rescuers Reach Isolated Villages
events.detail: By Sunday 16 August the confirmed death toll rose to 51 as search-and-rescue teams, previously blocked by landslides on the Trans-Flores highway, reached isolated villages in the epicentral zone for the first time.

events.title: Komodo National Park Treks and Snorkeling Resume
events.detail: Treks, viewpoints and snorkeling sites within Komodo National Park resumed operating on 16 August, a day after the tourism ministry confirmed park areas were 'under control'. Other sites — Wae Rebo, Ruteng Pu'u, Kelimutu National Park and the Maumere Bay Islands Marine Nature Park — remained closed.

events.title: M5.7–5.8 Aftershock Kills Two More in Ngada Regency
events.detail: A magnitude 5.7–5.8 aftershock struck Ngada Regency on 17 August, collapsing an already-weakened structure and killing two more people — a reminder that the aftershock sequence carried its own distinct fatality risk separate from the mainshock.

events.title: TNI/Polri Deployment Expands to 3,500 Personnel
events.detail: By 17 August roughly 3,500 members of TNI and Polri (National Police), including about 260 Mobile Brigade Corps personnel, had been dispatched to Manggarai, Maumere and other affected regencies, alongside specialized Basarnas search-and-rescue teams sent from Bali and West Nusa Tenggara.

events.title: Prabowo Leads Independence Day Moment of Silence for Flores Victims
events.detail: During Indonesia's 81st Independence Day ceremony in Jakarta on 17 August, President Prabowo Subianto asked participants to pray for people affected by the disaster in East Nusa Tenggara while leading a nationwide moment of silence, even as the observance continued on schedule.

events.title: Maumere Maritime Terminal Gangway Fails During Evacuation
events.detail: The maritime terminal building in Maumere (Sikka Regency) sustained major structural damage, and a gangway failed during a passenger evacuation, injuring several people trying to flee the port area.

events.title: Ruteng Regional Hospital's Operating Theatre Destroyed
events.detail: Ruteng Regional General Hospital sustained ceiling damage and its operating theatre was destroyed, forcing the evacuation of surgical patients even as the facility remained a treatment hub for quake casualties. Medical specialists were subsequently deployed from Surabaya to reinforce the Ruteng team.

events.title: Death Toll Reaches 54 on Independence Day
events.detail: Indonesia's earthquake death toll reached 54 on 17 August, Indonesia's Independence Day, with thousands still waiting for aid to reach isolated communities as national celebrations continued in Jakarta.

era: Aftershocks Persist, Aid Scales Up (18–19 August 2026)

events.title: Toll Rises to 68 as 12,800 Displaced
events.detail: BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan confirmed the death toll had risen to 68 by Monday 17–18 August, with 12,800 people displaced across Flores, many sheltering in schools, police stations and government-issued tents.

events.title: Toll Reaches 70, Displacement Surges Past 40,000
events.detail: Four days after the mainshock, the confirmed death toll rose to 70 and the number displaced surged to more than 40,000 as damage assessments extended to six regencies, with nearly 12,000 homes damaged.

events.title: Aftershock Count Reaches 2,119, BMKG Warns of Weeks of Shaking
events.detail: By 18 August BMKG had recorded 2,119 aftershocks since the mainshock, ranging from magnitude 1.1 to 6.2, prompting warnings that shaking would continue for weeks and complicating both rescue operations and residents' willingness to return to damaged homes.

events.title: BMKG: Aftershocks Likely to Continue 21–30 More Days
events.detail: As of 05:00 WIB on 19 August, BMKG had logged more than 2,768 aftershocks — 24 of them above magnitude 5.0 and 81 felt by residents — and predicted continued aftershock activity in East Nusa Tenggara for another 21 to 30 days, attributing the sequence to thrust-fault movement on the Flores Back-Arc Thrust.

events.title: NTT Governor Declares 14-Day State of Emergency
events.detail: East Nusa Tenggara Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena declared a 14-day provincial state of emergency, unlocking emergency budget authority and streamlining coordination of the multi-regency relief effort.

events.title: World Bank Pledges $50 Million in Emergency Funding
events.detail: The World Bank pledged $50 million in emergency recovery funding for Flores, conditional on a full damage assessment being completed by 25 August — one of the largest single international financial commitments announced so far.

events.title: Australia, Singapore Place SAR Teams on Standby; China, Iran Offer Aid
events.detail: Australian and Singaporean search-and-rescue teams were placed on standby, though Jakarta had not formally requested international deployment. China and Iran offered relief and medical assistance, the EU offered Copernicus satellite mapping support, and IFRC began preparing aid for roughly 2,000 people in temporary shelters. Singapore PM Lawrence Wong wrote directly to President Prabowo to convey condolences.

events.title: Power and Telecoms Near Full Restoration After Mass Outages
events.detail: The earthquake knocked out electricity to 566,797 people and disabled 812 cellular sites at its peak. By 19 August, the Ministry of Public Works reported telecommunications were 'nearly all restored' and power restoration was well underway, though remote hamlets remained without service.

events.title: Landslide on Kelimutu Crater Wall Closes National Park
events.detail: A landslide on the crater wall at Kelimutu National Park, famed for its tri-colored volcanic lakes, forced the closure of the site to visitors pending a geological safety assessment.

events.title: Only 32 of 52 Filling Stations Operating Island-Wide
events.detail: Only 32 of Flores' 52 fuel filling stations remained operational, with 20 shut due to power loss, structural damage or safety inspections — a bottleneck slowing relief-vehicle movement and generator refueling across the disaster zone.

events.title: Reports Emerge of Aid Failing to Reach Remote Villages
events.detail: Field reporting documented villages that had received no government assistance two days after the quake. One resident was quoted: 'As for help from the government, there hasn't been any — no tents, no medicine, no food, no drinking water, nothing.' Residents in several areas questioned why public kitchens had not yet been established.
events.confidenceReason: Single-outlet field reporting citing named residents; BNPB has not directly responded to these specific claims of villages receiving zero aid.

events.title: Quake Exposes Widespread Unsafe Housing Construction
events.detail: Analysis following the quake found nearly 80% of Indonesian residential buildings were constructed without engineering oversight or government supervision, and only about 11% of surveyed homes in the affected region met minimum earthquake-resistant standards. NTT's provincial government renovated just 436 homes in 2025 against a stated target of 5,000 for 2026.
events.confidenceReason: Figures drawn from a single advocacy-oriented outlet's analysis; not independently corroborated by official Indonesian housing ministry data in search results.

events.title: Basarnas Budget Cut Draws Criticism Amid Rescue Effort
events.detail: Critics noted that Indonesia's parliament had cut national search-and-rescue agency Basarnas's 2026 budget by 4.5% to Rp1.48 trillion, despite the agency's chief warning capacity needed to improve, not shrink. Basarnas operates only 38 offices across Indonesia's 514 regional jurisdictions. The cut was contrasted with a 30% increase in defense spending to Rp335.3 trillion under President Prabowo.
events.confidenceReason: Budget figures reported by a single politically-oriented outlet; framing of defense-vs-SAR tradeoff is contested by the government.

events.title: Confirmed Toll Reaches 73 Dead, 1,182 Injured
events.detail: As of 19 August, BNPB's confirmed toll stood at 73 dead and 1,182 injured from the mainshock, with two further deaths from the 17 August Ngada aftershock. Local search-and-rescue officials reported no further outstanding reports of people trapped or missing beneath rubble.
events.confidenceReason: Most recent official figure available; BNPB has cautioned totals may still be revised as assessments in remote hamlets continue.

events.title: Jakarta Post Editorial Urges Sustained National Attention
events.detail: In an editorial titled 'Pray for Flores', the Jakarta Post urged the government and public not to let attention fade once the initial rescue phase ended, warning that the harder work of rebuilding homes, schools and hospitals in one of Indonesia's poorer provinces was only beginning.

events.title: Geologists Note Same Fault That Killed 2,500 in 1992
events.detail: Seismologists confirmed the 2026 rupture occurred on the Flores Back-Arc Thrust, less than 40 km from the source of the catastrophic 1992 Flores earthquake and tsunami that killed roughly 2,500 people with run-ups of up to 26 metres. The 1992 event ruptured the thrust's eastern segment; the western segment — including the zone that ruptured in 2026 — has a long history of tsunamigenic quakes dating to at least 1800 (1815, 1857, 1917, 1979, 2018).

events.title: Two Cabinet Ministers Deliver Aid and Condolence Payments in Sikka
events.detail: Coordinating Minister for Food Affairs Zulkifli Hasan and Home Affairs Minister Tito Karnavian visited Sikka Regency on 19 August, distributing thousands of food-aid packages at Laurentius Say Port and Gelora Samadaor Stadium in Maumere and delivering condolence payments to bereaved families. Karnavian instructed local officials not to force residents back into damaged homes while aftershocks continue.

media.caption: Ministers Zulkifli Hasan and Tito Karnavian distribute aid in Sikka Regency

events.title: M5.8 Aftershock Triggers Fatal Heart Attack in Ruteng
events.detail: A magnitude 5.7–6.0 aftershock struck at 06:45 WITA on 20 August, and a resident near Ruteng Regional Hospital died of shock-induced cardiac arrest — the second fatality attributed to the aftershock sequence rather than the mainshock itself, after the 17 August Ngada deaths.

media.caption: Aftermath scene from the Flores earthquake zone, East Nusa Tenggara

events.confidenceReason: Aftershock magnitude reported inconsistently across outlets (5.8 vs 6.0); death itself corroborated by two sources.

events.title: Uncounted Flores Timur Death Surfaces Five Days Later
events.detail: A death that occurred on 15 August in Waiula Village, Wulanggitang District, Flores Timur Regency — a 74-year-old man who fell fatally while fleeing his home during the mainshock — only came to public attention on 20 August. The Flores Timur disaster agency said it had reported 'nil' casualties to the provincial command center, and the case exposed a gap: the regency never declared an emergency-response status, so its data was not being systematically collected alongside the eight regencies that had.

media.caption: Family of Mateus Noba Noba in Waiula Village, Flores Timur Regency

events.confidenceReason: Single regional outlet, but corroborated by direct quotes from the village head and the regency's own disaster response agency.

events.title: Toll Reaches 83 Dead, Displacement Tops 110,000, Aftershocks Pass 4,258
events.detail: As of 21 August 16:00 WIB, BPBD NTT and BNPB reported 83 confirmed deaths (up from 75 the previous day), 986 injured, and 110,785 displaced (up from 92,735 on 20 August). Homes damaged reached 44,946 (17,176 severely, 9,758 moderately, 18,013 slightly), concentrated in Manggarai, East Manggarai and West Manggarai regencies. BMKG recorded 4,258 aftershocks since the mainshock, ranging M1.1–M6.2, with 118 felt by residents. BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan said the newest deaths resulted from indirect impacts of the earthquake rather than building collapse.

media.caption: BPBD NTT casualty and damage tally infographic

events.confidenceReason: Most recent official BNPB/BPBD NTT figure, corroborated by three independent outlets; BNPB has cautioned counts remain provisional.
